claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 can be processed to exhibit a hierarchical heterostructure containing nanoscale precipitates embedded in a matrix.
The nanoprecipitate/matrix interfaces in the proposed HfNbTiVAl10 microstructure are coherent.
DFT-derived interfacial-energy descriptors can represent the mechanically relevant effects of the coherent interfaces.
A machine-learning surrogate can use interfacial descriptors and precipitate size, spacing, and coherence to calculate stress fields in place of full-field simulations.
Coherent nanoprecipitate/matrix interfaces govern dislocation nucleation in hierarchically structured HfNbTiVAl10.
The spatial distribution of hierarchical microstructural features governs crack propagation in HfNbTiVAl10.
The hierarchical structure creates local variations in stiffness.
The hierarchical structure creates local stress concentrations.
Nanoprecipitates and their interfaces contribute significantly to strengthening.
Nanoprecipitate/matrix interfaces contribute significantly to toughness.
Linking atomic-scale interfacial descriptors to macroscopic behavior with machine learning avoids simulation of full microstructural details.
Established full-field simulations require detailed microstructural reconstruction and intensive computation.
The integrated model will reduce prediction error for Young's modulus, tensile yield strength, and fracture-related properties by approximately 20% relative to established simulations.
The integrated model will reduce computation time by approximately 50% relative to established simulations.
Prediction performance may degrade when interfaces are irregular or incoherent or nanoprecipitates are distributed non-uniformly relative to the training data.
Unmodeled temperature-dependent mechanisms may cause the model to fail at elevated temperatures.
